_meta.indication: INVEGA (paliperidone) Extended-Release Tablets is indicated for the treatment of schizophrenia.

pivotal_trials.design: 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled (olanzapine), parallel-group, multicenter, fixed-dose study
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥ 18 years with a DSM-IV diagnosis of schizophrenia for at least 1 year, with a PANSS total score at screening and baseline of 70 to 120 points
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Day 43 in PANSS total score
pivotal_trials.n: Placebo N=126, 6 mg N=123, 9 mg N=122, 12 mg N=130, olanzapine 10 mg N=128
pivotal_trials.result: All paliperidone doses superior to placebo on PANSS (p<0.001); difference of LS means vs placebo: 6 mg -13.7, 9 mg -13.5, 12 mg -18.9

key_safety: Adverse events occurring at an incidence of 2% or more among INVEGA-treated patients and more frequent than placebo (pooled 3, 6, 9, 12 mg fixed-dose studies) included tachycardia (up to 14% across dose groups vs 7% placebo), headache (up to 14% vs 12% placebo), somnolence (up to 11% vs 7% placebo), and akathisia (up to 10% vs 4% placebo); the incidences of several adverse events, including somnolence, akathisia and extrapyramidal disorder, increased with dose.
target_moa: Paliperidone is the major active metabolite of risperidone; its therapeutic activity in schizophrenia is proposed to be mediated through a combination of central dopamine Type 2 (D2) and serotonin Type 2 (5HT2A) receptor antagonism.

boxed_warning.content: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis; atypical antipsychotics increase risk of death (1.6 to 1.7 times placebo; death rate ~4.5% vs ~2.6% placebo over 10 weeks). INVEGA is not approved for dementia-related psychosis.

advisory_committee.vote: FDA decided not to take this application to the Psychopharmacological Drugs Advisory Committee (PDAC).

description.text: Added treatment of schizoaffective disorder as monotherapy and as adjunct to mood stabilizers and/or antidepressants

citations.quote: These supplemental new drug applications provide for the use of Invega (paliperidone) extended release tablets for the treatment of schizoaffective disorder as monotherapy and as an adjunct to mood stabilizers and/or antidepressants.

basis.text: The original NDA review priority was Standard.

summary.text: INVEGA (paliperidone) was submitted as a 505(b) NDA received November 30, 2005 for the treatment of schizophrenia, under a standard review. An Approvable Letter was issued September 29, 2006; the sponsor's complete response submission of October 20, 2006 addressed the Agency's concerns, and the application was approved December 19, 2006. No advisory committee was convened.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated and received November 30, 2005, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Invega (paliperidone) 3, 6, 9, 12 mg Extended-Release Tablets.
The October 20, 2006 submission constituted a complete response to our September 29, 2006 action letter.
As noted, we decided not to take this application to the PDAC.

requirement.text: Repeat the pre- and postnatal developmental study in rats using doses that include a maximally tolerated dose for the dams.

citations.quote: The pre- and postnatal developmental study in rats did not use high enough doses to adequately evaluate the effects of paliperidone on this phase of reproduction. You have agreed to repeat the study in postmarketing using doses that include a maximally tolerated dose for the dams.

requirement.text: Within 3 months of approval, provide information addressing the possibility that ethanol might result in dose dumping, including solubility of coating materials in ethanol and data from other OROS formulations; if the possibility cannot be excluded, conduct a dissolution experiment in ethanolic solutions.

citations.quote: 2. You have agreed to, within 3 months of approval, provide information that addresses the possibility that ethanol might result in dose dumping. This should include information on the solubility of the coating materials in ethanol, and information from other similar OROS formulations. If such information cannot exclude the possibility of dose dumping and/or is not available, you have agreed to conduct a dissolution experiment in ethanolic solutions and provide the results.

requirement.text: Conduct a study to better explore for a minimal effective dose, as the lower end of the dose response curve was not fully evaluated.

citations.quote: 3. We note that in the one study that included a 3 mg dose of paliperidone ER, the dose was shown to be about as effective as higher doses. We therefore believe that you have not fully evaluated the lower end of the dose response curve. You have agreed to conduct a study to better explore for a minimal effective dose.
